summary: 失眠常见，但睡眠究竟为何必要仍有多种解释，包括整理记忆和维持生理功能。文章转入睡眠门诊，区分睡眠呼吸暂停与难以找到明显原因的失眠，并讨论睡眠习惯和认知行为疗法。

paragraphs.brief: 失眠的社会成本与研究缺口
sentences: Fifty-six million prescriptions for sleeping medication were handed out by doctors in America last year.
去年美国医生开出了五千六百万张安眠药处方。
Yet remarkably little is being done to understand insomnia’s root causes.
然而，用来查明失眠根源的研究却少得出奇。
Socially and economically, the undertreatment of sleeplessness is hugely expensive.
失眠未获充分治疗，让社会和经济都付出了巨大代价。
The Institute of Medicine, an independent scientific advisory group, estimates nearly 20 percent of all major accidents on the road are associated with driver sleepiness.
独立科学顾问机构医学研究所估计，近两成重大道路事故与驾驶员困倦有关。
The loss in terms of productivity within the workplace is even higher, costing billions.
工作场所因生产率下降造成的损失更高，达数十亿美元。
Then there are the softer costs which remain unmeasured but still exist; for example, the damaged relationships with others.
还有些代价不易计量，却同样存在，例如人际关系受损。

If other medical problems were causing such widespread harm, governments would act, but US authorities contribute only about $230 million a year for the funding of sleep research, comparable to the amount that the manufacturers of popular sleeping pills spent in three months on advertising.
如果其他健康问题造成如此广泛的危害，政府理应采取行动。然而，美国当局每年对睡眠研究的资助仅约 2.3 亿美元，与几种畅销安眠药的生产商三个月的广告开支相当。
Currently most medical school students get no more than four hours of training on sleep disorders; some get none.
目前多数医学生接受的睡眠障碍培训不超过四小时，有些人完全没受过这方面的训练。
paragraphs.gist: 美国一年开出五千六百万张安眠药处方，睡眠不足又牵涉车祸和生产损失，但研究经费与医学生接受的相关训练依然有限。

paragraphs.brief: 睡眠阶段已知，用途仍是谜
sentences: If we don’t know why we can’t sleep, it’s in part because we don’t really know why we need to sleep in the first place.
如果我们不知道为何不能入睡，部分是因为我们不知道为何必须入睡。
We know that we divide it between periods of deep-wave sleep and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, when the brain is as active as when we’re awake, but our voluntary muscles are paralyzed.
我们知道睡眠分为慢波深睡和快速眼动睡眠等阶段，快速眼动睡眠时大脑和清醒时一样活跃，随意肌却暂时不能活动。
We know that all mammals sleep, and that there are some insects and reptiles that only half sleep, in order to remain aware of their environment and predators.
我们知道所有哺乳动物都睡觉，还有些昆虫和爬行动物仅进入半睡状态，以便留意周围环境和天敌。
paragraphs.gist: 人们知道睡眠有慢波和快速眼动等阶段，也观察到有些动物睡时仍保持警觉，但睡眠本身为何必要仍未完全弄清。

paragraphs.brief: 不同睡眠阶段与两类学习
sentences: The predominant theory of sleep is that the brain demands it.
主流理论认为，睡眠是大脑的需要。
Recently, researchers at Harvard, led by Robert Stickgold, tested undergraduates on various aptitude tests, allowed them to nap, then tested them again.
最近，哈佛大学罗伯特·斯蒂克戈尔德带领的团队先让本科生做几项能力测验，在他们小睡后再测一次。
They found that those who had engaged in REM sleep subsequently performed better in pattern recognition tasks, such as grammar, while those who slept deeply were better at memorization.
经历快速眼动睡眠的人后来在语法等模式识别任务中表现较好，进入深睡的人则更善于记忆。
paragraphs.gist: 哈佛团队在学生小睡前后进行测试，发现经过快速眼动睡眠的人较善于识别规律，深睡者则更擅长记忆。

paragraphs.brief: 借清除冗余连接巩固记忆
sentences: Such studies suggest that memory consolidation may be one function of sleep.
这些研究表明，记忆的巩固可能是睡眠的一个功能。
Giulio Tononi, a sleep researcher at the University of Wisconsin, published an interesting twist on this theory a few years ago.
几年前，威斯康辛大学睡眠研究者朱利奥·托诺尼提出了一个不同角度的解释。
His study showed that the sleeping brain seems to delete redundant or unnecessary synapses or connections.
研究表明，人在睡眠中似乎会清除大脑里重复或不再需要的突触连接。
So the purpose of sleep may be to help us remember what’s important, by letting us forget what’s not.
睡眠或许是通过让我们忘记无关信息，来帮我们记住重要的内容。
paragraphs.gist: 托诺尼提出，睡眠中的大脑可能通过清除多余的神经连接，让人忘记不重要的信息，从而巩固重要记忆。

paragraphs.brief: 睡眠的生理作用尚无定论
sentences: Sleep is likely to have physiological purposes too.
睡眠很可能还有生理作用。
Some researchers have found that sleep deprivation impedes wound healing in rats, and others have suggested that sleep helps boost the immune system and control infection.
有研究发现缺乏睡眠会妨碍大鼠伤口愈合，也有研究者提出睡眠有助于增强免疫、防控感染。
But these studies are not conclusive.
不过，这些研究尚未得出定论。
At Stanford University, William Dement, co-founder of the Stanford Sleep Medicine Center, explains what he knows after 50 years of research, about the reason we sleep.
斯坦福大学睡眠医学中心联合创办人威廉·德门特谈起自己研究五十年后，对人为什么睡觉有何把握。
‘As far as I know,’ he said, ‘the only reason we need to sleep that is really, really solid is because we get sleepy.’
“据我所知，唯一真正可以肯定的理由，就是我们会犯困。”他说。
paragraphs.gist: 大鼠实验和免疫研究提示睡眠可能有助于伤口愈合和抵御感染，但这些结果仍不足以确定人为什么非睡不可。

paragraphs.brief: 用监测和面谈辨别睡眠障碍
sentences: The Stanford clinic does more than 3,000 overnight sleep studies a year.
斯坦福诊所每年进行3,000多次夜间睡眠研究。
Their main diagnostic tool is the polysomnogram, the main element of which is the electroencephalograph (EEG), which captures the electrical output from a patient’s brain.
他们的主要诊断工具是多导睡眠图，其中关键部分是记录患者脑电活动的脑电图。
As the EEG records a person’s sleep patterns, the polysomnogram technicians also measure body temperature, muscle activity, eye movement, and breathing.
脑电图记录睡眠模式的同时，技师还测量体温、肌肉活动、眼动和呼吸。
Then they look over the data for signs of abnormal sleep.
然后，他们查看数据以寻找异常睡眠的迹象。
When a person has narcolepsy, for instance, they plunge from wakefulness into REM sleep without any intermediate steps.
例如，发作性睡病患者会从清醒直接进入快速眼动睡眠，不经过中间阶段。
However, Clete Kushida, the clinic director, told me he can spot most people’s sleep problems right at the intake interview.
然而，诊所主任克莱特·库希达告诉我，他可以在接诊面谈时发现大多数人的睡眠问题。
‘There are those who cannot keep their eyes open, and those who just speak of their exhaustion but don’t actually fall asleep.
“有些人困得睁不开眼，另一些人虽诉说疲惫，却并不会睡着。
The former often have sleep apnea where they stop breathing.
前者常有睡眠呼吸暂停，睡着后呼吸会暂时停止。
The latter have true insomnia.’
后者才是真正的失眠。”
paragraphs.gist: 睡眠诊所用脑电和呼吸等数据寻找异常，主任也会在初诊区分困得睁不开眼的人和虽很疲惫却仍睡不着的人。

paragraphs.brief: 区分呼吸暂停与真正失眠
sentences: In sleep apnea, muscle relaxation allows the soft tissue of the throat to close, shutting off the sleeper’s air passage.
发生睡眠呼吸暂停时，肌肉松弛使咽部软组织塌陷，堵住气道。
When the brain realizes it is not getting oxygen, it sends a signal to the body to wake up.
大脑察觉缺氧，就向身体发出醒来的信号。
The sleeper awakes, inhales, and sleep returns.
睡眠者醒来吸一口气，接着又睡去。
Apnea is a serious problem but only indirectly a sleep disease.
呼吸暂停是严重问题，但它与睡眠本身的关系是间接的。
True insomniacs are people who either can’t get to, or can’t stay asleep for any evident reason.
真正的失眠者没有明显原因，却无法入睡，或睡着后不能保持睡眠。
paragraphs.gist: 睡眠呼吸暂停者是因咽部组织阻断气流、缺氧而醒来呼吸，典型失眠者则找不到明显原因，却仍难以入睡或维持睡眠。

paragraphs.brief: 气流装置与安眠药的局限
sentences: While apnea can be treated with a device that forces air down the sleeper’s throat to keep the airways open, the treatment of classic insomnia is not so clear cut.
睡眠呼吸暂停可用装置把气流送入咽喉，帮助气道保持通畅，典型失眠的治疗却没那么明确。
Acupuncture may help.
针灸也许能帮上忙。
It has long had this role in Asian medicine and is being studied at the University of Pittsburgh sleep center now.
在亚洲医学中，它长期用于助眠，匹兹堡大学睡眠中心目前也在开展相关研究。
Typically in the US, insomnia is treated in two ways.
美国通常采用两种方法治疗失眠。
First come the sleeping pills.
首先是使用安眠药。
Though safer than they once were, they can still lead to psychological addiction.
安眠药虽较过去安全，仍可能让人产生心理依赖。
‘Many users complain that their sleeping-pill sleep seems different, and they feel unfocused on waking.
“不少服用者觉得靠药物睡着和自然睡着不同，醒后也难以集中注意力。
Sleeping pills are not a natural way to sleep,’ points out Charles Czeisler, director of the Harvard Health and Safety Group.
安眠药提供的不是自然睡眠，”哈佛健康与安全小组主任查尔斯·蔡斯勒指出。
paragraphs.gist: 呼吸暂停可借气流维持气道通畅，失眠的治疗却较不明确，针灸仍在研究，常用安眠药还可能造成心理依赖。

paragraphs.brief: 认知行为疗法与患者感受
sentences: The second step in treating insomniacs is usually cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
治疗失眠症的第二步通常是认知行为疗法(CBT)。

In CBT, a psychologist teaches insomniacs to think about sleep problems as manageable, and to practice good ‘sleep hygiene’: sleep in a dark room, go to bed only when you are sleepy, don’t exercise beforehand.
在认知行为疗法中，心理学家帮助失眠者认识到睡眠问题可以应对，并指导他们养成良好的睡眠习惯：卧室保持黑暗，有睡意再上床，睡前避免运动。
Studies have shown that CBT is more effective than sleeping pills at treating long-term insomnia, but many sufferers aren’t convinced.
研究显示，CBT比安眠药在治疗长期失眠方面更有效，但许多患者不相信。
‘Some people continue in my experience to struggle,’ says John Winkelman, another sleep center director.
另一位睡眠中心主任约翰·温克尔曼说：“按我的经验，有些人仍然受到困扰。
‘They’re not super-satisfied with their sleep.’
他们对自己的睡眠还是谈不上满意。”
paragraphs.gist: 认知行为疗法借助对睡眠的看法和就寝习惯来改善长期失眠，研究中效果优于安眠药，但仍有患者对自己的睡眠不满意。

items.en: a mention of different cultural approaches to dealing with insomnia
items.zh: 不同文化如何应对失眠。
items.why: H 段同时介绍亚洲医学与美国对失眠的处理方式，说明不同文化和医疗体系如何应对同一问题。

items.en: indications that sleep has a positive effect on health
items.zh: 哪些迹象表明睡眠有益健康。
items.why: E段提到缺觉会妨碍大鼠伤口愈合，另有研究提示睡眠有助免疫和控制感染。

items.en: the effects of different kinds of sleep on mental performance
items.zh: 不同类型的睡眠如何影响认知表现。
items.why: 题干核心是 different kinds of sleep + mental performance。C段明确比较了 REM sleep 和 deep sleep 对不同认知任务的影响: 一个促进模式识别，一个促进记忆，所以选 C。

items.en: reasons why various species of animal sleep in different ways
items.zh: 各种动物以不同方式睡觉的原因
items.why: 题干要找的是“为什么不同物种睡眠方式不同”。 B段里不仅说到有些动物“half sleep”,还给出了原因: 为了保持对环境和天敌的警觉。因此完全对应。

items.en: the suggestion that sleep allows us to get rid of insignificant information
items.zh: 一种认为睡眠有助于清除不重要信息的看法。
items.why: D段提出通过遗忘不重要的信息来记住重要信息，正是睡眠清除次要信息的假说。

items.en: a description of how the brain responds when a person stops breathing
items.zh: 描述一个人停止呼吸时大脑的反应
items.why: 呼吸暂停导致缺氧时，大脑向身体发出醒来的信号，G段说明了这一反应。

items.en: Last year the high number of ________ doctors gave their patients highlights the fact that insomnia is a serious issue in the USA.
items.zh: 去年，医生给患者开出的________数量庞大，足以说明失眠在美国是个严重问题。
items.why: 医生向患者开出的是 prescriptions，即处方；原文用五千六百万张处方来说明美国失眠问题的规模。

items.en: It is evidently responsible for a number of serious traffic ________, and has a considerable effect on company ____ (Q16) A lack of sleep can also have a harmful effect on different relationships, although there are no statistics on this.
items.zh: 失眠显然导致了多起严重的交通________，对企业的________（Q16）也有很大影响。缺觉还可能损害人际关系，尽管这方面尚无统计数据。
items.why: 定位句说：“独立科学顾问机构医学研究所估计，近两成重大道路事故与驾驶员困倦有关。”

items.en: It is evidently responsible for a number of serious traffic ____ (Q15), and has a considerable effect on company ________ A lack of sleep can also have a harmful effect on different relationships, although there are no statistics on this.
items.zh: 失眠显然导致了多起严重的交通________（Q15），对企业的________也有很大影响。缺觉还可能损害人际关系，尽管这方面尚无统计数据。
items.why: 定位句说：“工作场所因生产率下降造成的损失更高，达数十亿美元。”

items.en: Unfortunately, there is insufficient official funding given to research into sleep problems, and the ________ given at medical school is also insufficient to deal with insomnia.
items.zh: 睡眠问题研究得到的政府资助不足，医学院提供的________也不足以应对失眠问题。
items.why: 定位句说：“目前多数医学生接受的睡眠障碍培训不超过四小时，有些人完全没受过这方面的训练。”

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Research tells us that we sleep as a reaction to our body’s signals.
items.zh: 研究表明，入睡是我们对身体发出的信号所作的反应。

items.en: People suffering from insomnia are easily recognisable.
items.zh: 失眠的人很容易辨认出来。

items.en: Therapy does not always enable people to achieve good quality sleep.
items.zh: 治疗未必总能让人获得高质量睡眠。

pairs: 删除多余或不重要的信息
points: E段提到缺觉会妨碍大鼠伤口愈合，另有研究提示睡眠有助免疫和控制感染。
医生向患者开出的是 prescriptions，即处方；原文用五千六百万张处方来说明美国失眠问题的规模。
clauses: Then there are the softer costs … ; for example, the damaged relationships with others.
“which remain unmeasured but still exist”修饰前面的 costs。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 costs，再把修饰信息接回主句。

…, governments would act, but US authorities contribute only about $230 million a year for the funding of sleep research, comparable to the amount that the manufacturers of popular sleeping pills spent in three months on advertising.
连接词 if 引出“If other medical problems were causing such widespread harm”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Insomnia, the inability to fall and stay asleep, is at epidemic levels.
失眠包括难以入睡和睡着后难以保持睡眠，如今已十分普遍。
If sleep is so important to us, why is it sometimes so hard to achieve?
如果睡眠对我们来说如此重要，为什么有时很难做到呢？
vocabulary: 随意肌；能自主控制的肌肉
